channel.title: ForgeDITA Blog
channel.description: DITA architecture, conformance, publishing, and operations.

item.title: Publishing Drift Is an Architecture Problem
item.description: Why DITA publishing environments drift, why procedural discipline cannot fully contain the problem, and how versioned toolchains restore control.

item.title: What a Public DITA Conformance Statement Should Contain
item.description: A practical model for specific, testable, versioned DITA conformance claims that include limitations instead of hiding them.

item.title: Why Your DITA Content May Not Be as Portable as You Think
item.description: Native XML is necessary for portability, but catalogs, grammars, plugins, semantics, and publishing profiles also determine whether content can actually move.

item.title: The CCMS Dependency Graph: From File Storage to Content Infrastructure
item.description: Why maps, keys, conrefs, subject schemes, and reuse relationships require a contextual dependency graph rather than file-oriented storage alone.

item.title: Why Toolchain Bundles Must Be Versioned and Immutable
item.description: How immutable tenant toolchain bundles reduce publishing drift, isolate customers, and make historical releases rebuildable.

item.title: Seven Questions to Ask During a CCMS Demonstration
item.description: Seven demonstration requests that reveal CCMS portability, contextual resolution, reproducibility, failure behavior, and operational maturity.
